bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing enterprise customer relationships — two customers each contributed more than 10% of Group revenue in both FY26 and FY25, indicating deep but concentrated accounts
- Direct US market access following the acquisition of Elite Computer Consultants, L.P. through IT CATS LLC, which management states strengthens market presence and service delivery capability in North America
- Proprietary Digital DAIS™ integrated digital transformation framework used to deliver technology-led business solutions
- Net cash position — as at 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2025 the Group's cash and cash equivalents exceeded its debt including lease liabilities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — Two customers each contributed more than 10% of Group revenue in FY26 and again in FY25, so the loss or ramp-down of a single account can move consolidated revenue materially. Sourced from the operating-segment note in the profile bundle of the same annual report.
- Operating leverage on a falling revenue base — Standalone revenue fell about 14.23% in FY26 and management states major operating costs could not be reduced in the same proportion as the decline in revenue, so profitability and return ratios deteriorated sharply. A services cost base that is largely fixed people cost amplifies any revenue shortfall.
- Delayed discretionary technology spending and pricing pressure — Management explicitly flags delayed discretionary spending and pricing pressures alongside global macroeconomic uncertainties and geopolitical developments as continuing industry challenges, which directly compress a mid-size IT services vendor's win rates and realisations.
- Talent acquisition, attrition and reskilling cost — Increasing competition for specialized digital talent is flagged, and the rapid pace of AI adoption may alter traditional workforce models and require continuous investments in reskilling and capability enhancement. With 165 employees, the company has limited bench depth to absorb this.
- Structural shift from headcount-led to productivity-led growth — The industry is in a structural transition from headcount-led growth to productivity-led and innovation-led growth models. For a staffing-and-services provider this threatens the revenue-per-head model unless domain expertise, AI-enabled delivery and cloud capabilities are combined effectively.
- Foreign currency exposure on US-denominated receivables — The Company operates internationally and has transactional currency exposures mainly in US Dollars, with unhedged trade receivable balances denominated in USD at each reporting date. Sourced from the financial-risk-management note in the registry bundle of the same annual report.
- Geographic and integration risk in the US subsidiary chain — Growth is concentrated in a US step-down subsidiary stack (IT CATS LLC holding Sapplica INC, Sarral Global INC and Elite Computer Consultants L.P.), with goodwill and acquired customer-contract intangibles carried against it and an intangible-asset impairment recognised at the consolidated level in FY26.
- Information security and technology obsolescence — The Company has constituted a Security Management Group and its risk assessment procedure begins with identification of critical information assets across functions, indicating that data and information-asset security is a primary managed risk for the business.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Sagarsoft is an asset-light IT services and staffing business and discloses no manufacturing capacity or plant-level capex programme. Its expansion during the year was inorganic and geographic rather than physical: its wholly owned US subsidiary IT CATS LLC acquired a 51% stake in Sarral Global INC, USA, making it a step-down subsidiary, adding to IT CATS LLC's existing 60% holding in Sapplica INC and 100% holding in Elite Computer Consultants L.P. The Elite Computer Consultants acquisition (control obtained effective 28 February 2025) was undertaken to gain direct access to U.S. customers and strengthen market presence and service delivery capability in North America. Capability build-out is described as investment in Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Data Engineering, Cloud Modernization, Automation and Cybersecurity, plus training programmes for the 165 employees on roll as at 31 March 2026. No commissioning, ramp or completion timeline for any capital project is disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian technology industry is expected to grow by approximately 6.1% in FY2026-27, with industry revenues projected to reach nearly USD 315 billion, driven by AI-led transformation, cloud modernization, engineering R&D services, cybersecurity and Global Capability Centres
- GCC expansion continued at pace, with India hosting over 2,100 GCCs serving global enterprises across BFSI, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, telecom and engineering
- Technology spending continues to shift towards enterprise software, cloud infrastructure, data engineering, cybersecurity and AI-enabled solutions
- Generative AI and Agentic AI emerged as a major transformation driver, with enterprises moving from pilots to scalable AI deployments
- Demand is expected to remain strong in cloud transformation, cybersecurity, data engineering, AI integration, digital engineering and managed services
- Headwinds flagged: global macroeconomic uncertainties, geopolitical developments, delayed discretionary spending, pricing pressures, evolving regulatory requirements and competition for specialised digital talent
- The industry is in a structural transition from headcount-led growth to productivity-led and innovation-led growth models, which may alter traditional workforce models and require continuous reskilling investment
- FY26 ratio deterioration was attributed to lower revenue from operations with major operating costs not reducing in the same proportion, adversely impacting profitability

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Indian technology industry is expected to grow by approximately 6.1% in FY2026-27, with industry revenues projected to reach nearly USD 315 billion, driven by AI-led transformation, cloud modernization, engineering R&D services, cybersecurity and Global Capability Centres
- GCC expansion continued at pace, with India hosting over 2,100 GCCs serving global enterprises across BFSI, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, telecom and engineering
- Technology spending continues to shift towards enterprise software, cloud infrastructure, data engineering, cybersecurity and AI-enabled solutions
- Generative AI and Agentic AI emerged as a major transformation driver, with enterprises moving from pilots to scalable AI deployments
- Demand is expected to remain strong in cloud transformation, cybersecurity, data engineering, AI integration, digital engineering and managed services
- Headwinds flagged: global macroeconomic uncertainties, geopolitical developments, delayed discretionary spending, pricing pressures, evolving regulatory requirements and competition for specialised digital talent
- The industry is in a structural transition from headcount-led growth to productivity-led and innovation-led growth models, which may alter traditional workforce models and require continuous reskilling investment
- FY26 ratio deterioration was attributed to lower revenue from operations with major operating costs not reducing in the same proportion, adversely impacting profitability

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strengthen digital capabilities and enhance operational agility to address evolving customer requirements in a rapidly changing technology landscape
- Keep strategic priorities centred on Applications, Infrastructure, Data & Analytics, Cloud, AI-enabled transformation and Cybersecurity services
- Deliver technology-led business solutions through the Digital DAIS™ integrated digital transformation framework using a 'Business First' approach
- Invest in emerging technology capabilities — Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Data Engineering, Cloud Modernization, Automation and Cybersecurity
- Strengthen customer relationships and expand service capabilities across key industry verticals
- Improve delivery efficiency through automation and innovation-led execution models
- Build scalable, future-ready solutions for outcome-based digital transformation programs
- Expand North American presence through the US subsidiary chain — IT CATS LLC acquired a 51% stake in Sarral Global INC during the year, adding to Sapplica INC (60%) and Elite Computer Consultants L.P. (100%)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Sagarsoft is an asset-light IT services and staffing business and discloses no manufacturing capacity or plant-level capex programme. Its expansion during the year was inorganic and geographic rather than physical: its wholly owned US subsidiary IT CATS LLC acquired a 51% stake in Sarral Global INC, USA, making it a step-down subsidiary, adding to IT CATS LLC's existing 60% holding in Sapplica INC and 100% holding in Elite Computer Consultants L.P. The Elite Computer Consultants acquisition (control obtained effective 28 February 2025) was undertaken to gain direct access to U.S. customers and strengthen market presence and service delivery capability in North America. Capability build-out is described as investment in Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Data Engineering, Cloud Modernization, Automation and Cybersecurity, plus training programmes for the 165 employees on roll as at 31 March 2026. No commissioning, ramp or completion timeline for any capital project is disclosed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-standing enterprise customer relationships — two customers each contributed more than 10% of Group revenue in both FY26 and FY25, indicating deep but concentrated accounts
- Direct US market access following the acquisition of Elite Computer Consultants, L.P. through IT CATS LLC, which management states strengthens market presence and service delivery capability in North America
- Proprietary Digital DAIS™ integrated digital transformation framework used to deliver technology-led business solutions
- Net cash position — as at 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2025 the Group's cash and cash equivalents exceeded its debt including lease liabilities

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration — Two customers each contributed more than 10% of Group revenue in FY26 and again in FY25, so the loss or ramp-down of a single account can move consolidated revenue materially. Sourced from the operating-segment note in the profile bundle of the same annual report.
- Operating leverage on a falling revenue base — Standalone revenue fell about 14.23% in FY26 and management states major operating costs could not be reduced in the same proportion as the decline in revenue, so profitability and return ratios deteriorated sharply. A services cost base that is largely fixed people cost amplifies any revenue shortfall.
- Delayed discretionary technology spending and pricing pressure — Management explicitly flags delayed discretionary spending and pricing pressures alongside global macroeconomic uncertainties and geopolitical developments as continuing industry challenges, which directly compress a mid-size IT services vendor's win rates and realisations.
- Talent acquisition, attrition and reskilling cost — Increasing competition for specialized digital talent is flagged, and the rapid pace of AI adoption may alter traditional workforce models and require continuous investments in reskilling and capability enhancement. With 165 employees, the company has limited bench depth to absorb this.
- Structural shift from headcount-led to productivity-led growth — The industry is in a structural transition from headcount-led growth to productivity-led and innovation-led growth models. For a staffing-and-services provider this threatens the revenue-per-head model unless domain expertise, AI-enabled delivery and cloud capabilities are combined effectively.
- Foreign currency exposure on US-denominated receivables — The Company operates internationally and has transactional currency exposures mainly in US Dollars, with unhedged trade receivable balances denominated in USD at each reporting date. Sourced from the financial-risk-management note in the registry bundle of the same annual report.
- Geographic and integration risk in the US subsidiary chain — Growth is concentrated in a US step-down subsidiary stack (IT CATS LLC holding Sapplica INC, Sarral Global INC and Elite Computer Consultants L.P.), with goodwill and acquired customer-contract intangibles carried against it and an intangible-asset impairment recognised at the consolidated level in FY26.
- Information security and technology obsolescence — The Company has constituted a Security Management Group and its risk assessment procedure begins with identification of critical information assets across functions, indicating that data and information-asset security is a primary managed risk for the business.
